Hi Tom — thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed around security/compliance and data lifecycle so your team (and procurement) can move forward: 

Key points we covered
- SOC 2 status: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II in final audit (Type I completed); we can share the current Type II report under NDA.
- GDPR/HIPAA: Platform supports data residency controls; we offer BAA and standard DSAs for PHI workflows.
- Retention & deletion: default application logs retained 90 days; customer-configurable TTLs available for stored artifacts (embeddings, audit logs).
- Backups & snapshots: periodic backups are taken for platform state; backups are encrypted and have a 30–90 day retention depending on customer plan.
- Deletion SLA: we typically honor data deletion requests within 30 days of a verified request; for backups, we can commit to an erase window of up to 90 days depending on snapshot cadence and RPO.

Attachments: Redwood_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_Fillable.pdf (fillable VSA) and a high-level Retention_SLA_Table.xlsx that maps product artifacts to retention defaults and SLA ranges.

Action items / next steps
1) Tom / Procurement: share your vendor questionnaire and any specific deletion SLA horizon you need for backups (e.g., 30-day vs 90-day).
2) Rishi: will prepare a short summary on backups/snapshot cadence and confirm the technical erase flow for snapshots.
3) Priyom: please draft a BAA addendum example we can surface to CareNet if they need HIPAA language.
4) Neha: I'll pull the latest SOC 2 Type II report and upload to the secure ShareFile link once NDA is in place.

Tom — can you confirm who in your team will own the vendor questionnaire? Also let me know if procurement needs us to route the SOC 2 via an external portal (e.g., ShareFile / SecureDocs).

Looping in high-level answers — I'll produce a short tech note for procurement, but here's the summary we can share to align expectations: 

Backups & snapshots (Hosted API vs Dedicated)
- Hosted (standard): application-level logs and ephemeral caches: default retention 90d. Nightly system snapshots retained 30 days; immutable snapshot lifecycle means deletion requests are applied to primary data immediately, but snapshot residuals may remain until snapshot expiry — typical upper bound = 30 days. We can commit to a documented 30-day snapshot residual for Hosted.
- Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pools): customers can opt-in for more frequent snapshotting and shorter snapshot retention. For Dedicated SLA we can offer: snapshot cadence configurable (daily/4hr), and an erase-window cap of 45 days for snapshot residuals as a contractual maximum; operationally we aim for <=14 days for most customers depending on snapshot replication and cross-region backups.

RPO / RTO
- Hosted: RPO best-effort; not suitable for sub-2-hour RTO guarantees.
- Dedicated: we can commit to RTO <= 2 hours for critical endpoints as part of a Dedicated SLA (requires reserved capacity and defined failover routing). RPO targets depend on snapshot cadence; with 4hr snapshots RPO ~4 hours.

Deletion flow for backups
1) Customer submits deletion request (verified).
2) Primary dataset is logically deleted within 24–48 hours.
3) Background purge initiates; for Hosted the purge removes references but physical copies in snapshots remain until snapshot expiry. For Dedicated we can prioritize and do targeted snapshot scrubs; documented maximum residual window will be contractual.

KMS / encryption / audit logs
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest and TLS1.3 in transit. KMS integrations available (Cloud KMS / customer-managed keys) for Dedicated.
- Audit logs: admin and API audit logs retained 365 days by default for Dedicated customers; Hosted customers retain 90 days. We can surface admin audit exports to procurement under S3/ShareFile link.

I'll get the write-up and a suggested SLA paragraph by EOD Monday (2027-05-09) so Neha can include it in the procurement response.

Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
